verdicts.title: Vertex elimination orderings for hereditary graph classes
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We provide a general method to prove the existence and compute efficiently elimination orderings in graphs. Our method relies on several tools that were known before, but that were not put together so far: the algorithm LexBFS due to Rose, Tarjan and Lueker, one of its properties discovered by Berry and Bordat, and a local decomposition property of graphs discovered by Maffray, Trotignon and Vu\vsković. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses vertex elimination orderings in graphs and their applications to graph classes, but does not mention cumulative entropy, resolution proof complexity, or Tseitin formulas, which are central to the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Exact and approximate inference in graphical models: variable elimination and beyond
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Probabilistic graphical models offer a powerful framework to account for the dependence structure between variables, which is represented as a graph. However, the dependence between variables may render inference tasks intractable. In this paper we review techniques exploiting the graph structure for exact inference, borrowed from optimisation and computer science. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses variable elimination orders, treewidth, and algorithms for exact and approximate inference in graphical models. It does not specifically address the comparison of Φ under a BAD elimination order (max-occurrence) to Φ under min-occurrence or their order-sensitivity with respect to cumulative entropy.

At each round a pair of players is chosen (uniformly at random) and a fair coin flip is made resulting in the transfer of one unit between these two players.
